transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

I guess the main thing is I’m just… exhausted. Like, not normal tired after a long day, but this heavy kind of tired where I can barely make it through my shift at the register. I’m standing there trying to scan things and talk to customers and it feels like my whole body is packed with wet sand, if that makes sense. Everything takes so much effort.

And the weird part is, resting doesn’t really fix it. I’ll sit down, or I’ll try to take it easy when I’m off, and I still don’t feel like I get my energy back. It’s been bad enough that I finally thought, okay, I probably need to come in and talk to someone, because I can’t keep pushing through like this.
How long has this feeling of exhaustion been going on?

It’s been about a month now, I think. It kind of started around when the store changed our hours because of the remodel. At first I thought it was just the schedule being weird and my body not adjusting, you know, like maybe I was just thrown off for a week or two. But it didn’t really let up. It’s been this whole stretch since then, pretty much every day, and now it feels like it’s gone on long enough that I can’t just blame the remodel hours anymore.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, socializing, or other activities?

Yeah… yeah, I have. That’s actually been one of the things that feels the most wrong to me, because it’s not like I don’t have things I normally like. I usually love cooking for myself — like making a real meal, trying little recipes, putting music on while I do it — and lately it just feels like a chore, or like cardboard. I’ll stand there looking at ingredients and think, why bother?

Same with guitar. I used to pick it up without even thinking, just to mess around for a while, and now I’ll see it sitting there and I just… don’t feel anything. Hiking too, which normally clears my head, and even going over to my family’s place. I know I care about them, I know I usually enjoy being around them, but right now it all feels flat, like I’m only pretending to be interested so nobody notices how off I feel.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just feeling exhausted or losing interest in things?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. I mean… I know I don’t feel like myself, and I feel kind of flat and worn down a lot of the time, but when you say “down” I’m not sure. It’s not like I’m crying all day or thinking, “I’m so sad,” every minute.

It’s more like everything feels heavy and muted, if that makes sense. Like I’m going through the motions and I’m not getting much back from anything. But I don’t know if that counts as depressed most of the day. I guess I haven’t really been tracking it that way.
Would you say that most days, you feel down or sad for most of the day, even if it's not intense sadness?

I’m honestly not sure. I keep trying to fit it into that word, like “sad,” and it doesn’t feel exactly right. Most days I do feel… low, I guess, or dimmed down. Like everything takes more effort and I’m not really excited about anything, but I don’t always have this obvious sadness where I could point to it and say, yes, that’s what it is.

There are parts of the day where I’m just distracted or I’m working and I’m not thinking about how I feel, so I don’t know if that counts as feeling down most of the day. But when I stop and check in with myself, it’s usually not good. It’s not like I wake up feeling bright and then it passes. It’s more like this dull, heavy background feeling that’s been there a lot, but I don’t know how to measure whether it’s “most of the day” or just… kind of always hanging around.
Can you think back over the past few days — was there any time when you actually felt in a better mood, even for a little while, or did you feel low or flat throughout most of the day, every day?

I’m trying to think through it honestly. The past few days kind of blur together, which makes it hard to answer cleanly. I wouldn’t say there were these clear periods where I felt genuinely good, like, “Oh, there I am, I’m back.” It’s more that there were moments where I was distracted enough that I wasn’t actively noticing how flat I felt.

Like if something at work needed my attention, or I was scrolling on my phone, or someone said something and I had to respond, I could seem normal for a bit. I might even laugh at something, but it didn’t really feel like my mood lifted in a real way. It was more like the feeling got covered up for a second.

So… I think most of the day, most days, it’s been low or flat in the background. I’m still not sure if I’d call it “sad” exactly, but I don’t remember any real stretch recently where I felt lighter or actually better. It’s just been kind of there, dragging along underneath everything.
Would you say that over the last two weeks, you’ve had days where you felt down or in a low mood for most of the day, even if it wasn’t intense sadness?

Yeah… I think so, but I’m still a little unsure how to say it the right way. Over the last two weeks, there have definitely been days where I felt low for most of the day, even if it wasn’t like this sharp, obvious sadness. It’s more like this gray feeling, like I’m just kind of under everything, if that makes sense.

I wouldn’t say every minute of every day I’m sitting there thinking, “I’m depressed,” because sometimes I’m busy or I’m talking to someone or just trying to get through work, and then I’m not focused on it. But when I think back on the days overall, a lot of them had that same low, flat feeling running through them. Like I could function, but it didn’t feel like I was really okay underneath.

So… yes, I guess I would say I’ve had days like that over the last couple weeks. It just hasn’t always felt like sadness in the way I imagine sadness is supposed to feel.
Over the past two weeks, would you say that on most days, you've felt down or in a low mood for most of the day, even if it wasn’t intense sadness?

I know I’m kind of circling the same answer, but… I don’t think I can say it with total confidence the way you’re asking it. Like, “most days” and “most of the day” feels hard for me to judge, because I don’t keep track hour by hour, and sometimes I’m just going through the motions and not really checking in with myself.

What I can say is that when I look back over the last couple weeks, a lot of the days have felt low or flat overall. Not dramatic sadness exactly, not always crying or anything like that, but just this heavy, muted feeling. Like I can still do things and answer people and get through whatever I’m supposed to do, but underneath it I don’t feel right.

So… yes, probably on most days it’s been there for a good part of the day, but I’m saying “probably” because I’m not sure how precise I’m being. It’s more like the general tone of the days has been low.
Over the past two weeks, would you say that on most days, you’ve had a low or depressed mood for the majority of the day, even if it wasn’t intense sadness?

I’m not completely sure how to pin it down that neatly. I know I’ve been saying it’s been low or flat, and that’s true in a general way, but when you ask “most days” and “majority of the day,” I get stuck because I don’t really measure it like that while it’s happening.

There are times during the day when I’m just doing what I have to do, like getting through tasks or answering people, and in those moments I might not be thinking, “I feel depressed right now.” But then when there’s quiet, or when I look back at the day, it feels like the low feeling was sort of sitting there underneath most of it.

So… I think the honest answer is probably yes, but I don’t want to say it like I’m totally certain. It hasn’t been intense sadness all the time. It’s more like a dull, heavy, flat mood that’s been around a lot, and I don’t really remember many days lately where I felt okay for most of the day.
Over the past two weeks, would you say that on most days, you’ve had a low or depressed mood for the majority of the day, even if it wasn’t intense sadness?

I mean… I guess I don’t have a cleaner answer than what I’ve been trying to say. I don’t know if I can honestly count it out and say, yes, exactly most days and exactly most of the day, because I don’t really notice it in that organized a way while I’m living through it.

It’s more like, if I’m at work or I’m dealing with people, I can get through it and I might not be actively thinking, “I’m depressed.” I’m just scanning groceries, answering questions, doing whatever I’m supposed to do. But then when I get a quiet moment, or when I think back on the day, it feels like that low feeling was there underneath things a lot of the time.

So… probably yes, but I’m saying probably because I don’t want to overstate it. It hasn’t been like nonstop crying or anything that obvious. It’s more like the days have had this dull, heavy tone to them, and I haven’t really had many days lately where I’d say I felt okay for most of the day.
Over the past two weeks, would you say that most days, your mood was depressed — like feeling sad, empty, or hopeless — for most of the day, even if it wasn’t very intense?

I’m still not totally sure how to answer that in a clean yes-or-no way. I know you’re trying to get at whether it’s been there most days and most of the day, and I don’t want to dodge the question, but I also don’t want to sound more certain than I am.

It’s not like I wake up and say, “I’m hopeless,” and then feel that exact thing every minute until I go to bed. A lot of the time I’m just kind of… moving through the day. I can be at the register, talking to customers, doing normal things, and I’m not always labeling it as sadness in the moment. But when I step back, the days do feel pretty empty or flat, like there isn’t much lift in them.

So I guess I’d say… maybe, probably, but I’m not confident enough to say it like it’s definite. It hasn’t been intense all the time. It’s more that things have felt kind of muted and heavy, and I don’t really have a lot of recent days I’d point to and say, “That was a good mood day.”
Over the past two weeks, would you say that on more days than not, you felt down or in a low mood for the majority of the day, even if it wasn’t intense sadness?

I’m sorry, I feel like I’m giving you the same messy answer over and over, but I really don’t know how to make it more exact than that.

But looking back over the last couple weeks, I don’t remember many days where I felt light or normal for most of the day. It’s more like this low, flat feeling has been around in the background a lot, even if I’m not sitting there actively feeling sad every second. So… I think maybe yes, but I’m saying that carefully, because it’s not like I can point to a chart in my head and be sure.
Looking back over the past two weeks, would you say that on more days than not, you felt down, low, or in a depressed mood for the majority of the day, even if it wasn’t intense or obvious sadness?

I know I’ve kind of circled around this already, and I’m sorry. I think the most honest answer is that I’m not completely sure how to measure it.

Like, if you asked me, “Were you crying or feeling obviously depressed all day?” then no, not like that. But if you mean this heavier, lower feeling kind of being there underneath things, then… yeah, I think it’s been there more often than not. I just don’t always notice it while I’m busy, so it’s hard for me to say “for the majority of the day” with total confidence.

Looking back, though, I don’t really remember many days in the last two weeks where I felt normal or genuinely okay for most of the day. It’s more like I’ve been functioning, but with this low mood in the background. So I’d say probably yes, but not in a neat, obvious way.

Looking back, do you think there were more days than not in the past two weeks when you felt low or down for the larger part of the day, even if it wasn’t intense sadness?

I hear what you’re asking, and I know you’re trying to pin it down. I just… I still don’t know if I can honestly say yes to that exact wording.

Then later I’ll think, “I didn’t feel good today,” but I don’t know if that means most of the day or just parts of it.

So I guess my answer is: maybe, but I’m not confident. It’s been there enough to notice, but I can’t say for sure that it was more days than not for most of the day.

I think my honest answer is still that I don’t know how to call it exactly. I’m not trying to be difficult, I promise. It’s just that the way you’re asking it has those parts to it — “more days than not” and “majority of the day” — and I don’t feel like I can look back and measure that cleanly.

So… I’d say it’s possible, but I’m not confident enough to say yes. It’s been kind of mixed and hard for me to pin down.

I know I’ve kind of circled around this a few times, and I’m sorry. I think the truest answer is still that I’m not sure. So I guess I’d say… I don’t know. Maybe some days, yes, but I can’t honestly say it was more days than not for most of the day.
